\begin{gathered}\forall n : \mathbb{N},\ \forall a : \mathbb{N},\ \forall b : \mathbb{N},\ \forall c : \mathbb{N},\ 2 < n \\ \implies (0 < a \\ \implies (0 < b \\ \implies (0 < c \\ \implies a^{n} + b^{n} \neq c^{n})))\end{gathered}
\forall p : \mathbb{N},\ \forall a : \mathbb{Z},\ \operatorname{Prime}(p) \implies a^{p} \equiv a \pmod{p}
